title_en: Cosmic Buddha Vairochana with the Realms of Existence
current_location: Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian (National Museum of Asian Art), Washington, DC
description: A larger-than-life standing figure (missing head and both hands) carved in a pillar-like form and wearing a simple monk's robe. Every inch of the robe is filled with relief carvings; the front shows a symbolic map of the Buddhist universe — the Realms of Existence: divinities beneath the neck, Mount Meru as a pillar wrapped with dragons, the realms of humans, animals, spirits, and Buddhist hells distributed from waist to feet.

title_zh: 诸佛与菩萨集会图(响堂山中心柱浮雕)
provenance_or_findsite: Southern Xiangtangshan, probably Cave 2, Hebei province, China
current_location: Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian, Washington, DC
description: Relief-sculpture mural that most likely once decorated a stupa-pillar attached to the center of the rear wall of one of the caves at Southern Xiangtangshan, a court-sponsored Buddhist cave-temple created during the Northern Qi dynasty. Several scholars suggest the mural came from Cave 2. Acquired through Lai-Yuan & Company, New York in 1921; damaged in transit and repaired in late 1922.

title_en: Western Paradise of the Buddha Amitabha
provenance_or_findsite: Southern Xiangtangshan Buddhist cave-temple site, Cave 2
current_location: Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian, Washington, DC
description: Mural showing Amitabha presiding over a pond and welcoming newly reborn souls emerging from lotus blossoms — among the earliest known depictions of the Western Paradise in Chinese art. From the Southern Xiangtangshan Buddhist cave-temple site, Cave 2.

title_zh: 胁侍菩萨立像(响堂山第二窟)
provenance_or_findsite: Cave 2, Southern Xiangtangshan, Hebei province, China
current_location: Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian, Washington, DC (Gift of Agnes E. Meyer, 1968)
description: Originally located in Cave 2, southern Xiangtangshan, Hebei province, China. From at least 1916 to 1968 in the collection of Eugene Meyer and Agnes E. Meyer, purchased from C. T. Loo not later than 13 March 1916; given to the Freer Gallery in 1968.

title_en: The Bodhisattva Mile (Sanskrit Maitreya), seated in "Pensive Pose"
current_location: Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian, Washington, DC
description: Stone sculpture of the Bodhisattva Maitreya seated in the 'pensive pose' (思惟相), characteristic of Northern Qi (6th-century) Buddhist sculpture.

title_zh: 维摩诘与文殊菩萨论辩造像碑
title_en: Buddhist stele depicting debate between Weimo and Wenshu
current_location: Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian, Washington, DC
description: Buddhist stele depicting the debate between Vimalakirti (Chinese Weimo / 维摩诘) and Manjusri (Wenshu / 文殊).

title_zh: 三世佛造像碑(过去、现在、未来)
title_en: Stele with Buddhas of the Past, Present and Future
current_location: Freer Gallery of Art, Smithsonian, Washington, DC
description: Stele depicting the Three Buddhas (Past, Present, Future) — a common Northern dynasties Buddhist iconography.
